title: Uncertain at an observed point?
hook: Condition a fixed one-point Gaussian process.

doesNotKnow: Zero-mean GP: k(x,z)=exp(−(x−z)²/2), observed (0,1). With noise variance 1, must latent variance at x=0 vanish?

objective: Compute the gaussian process uncertainty finite model and explain its changed countercase and stated boundary.

claims.text:
3. gaussian-process-uncertainty

Target / packet: ai-gaussian-process-uncertainty · P2. Prerequisites: ai:bayesian-posterior-lines.

Nearest / distinct payoff: bayesian-posterior-lines → ai-bayesian-posterior-lines. Finite candidate lines are not a kernel process; here the full one-observation Gaussian conditional is computed with a declared covariance kernel.

Finite primary model: Zero-mean GP prior kernel k(x, z)=exp(-(x-z)^2/2), one observation x=0, y=1. With noise variance 0 posterior mean=k(x,0), latent variance 1-k(x,0)^2. At x=0:1,0; at x=sqrt(2 ln 2):.5,.75.

Countercase and mathematical boundary: Noise variance 1 changes formula to mean=k/2, latent variance 1-k²/2; at observed x=0 mean=.5, variance=.5. New-observation variance additionally includes noise 1. Kernel/length scale fixed, no fitted hyperparameters.

Predict and recall transfer: Predict whether uncertainty vanishes at a noisy observation; recall far-away k→0 yields prior mean 0, variance 1.

Required observable evidence: Show one observed point and two query locations with explicitly labeled latent variance; no arbitrary shaded bands implying coverage.

Source obligation: [Rasmussen–Williams author textbook chapter2](https://gaussianprocess.org/gpml/chapters/RW2.pdf), acquired PDF index9–10, eq2.23–2.26 posterior mean/covariance; index11 distinguishes noisy predictions. [Maintainer GPR formulation](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/gaussian_process.htmlregression) also acquired. Use exact one-point conditioning, no copied figure or claim about fitted real-world uncertainty.
